claims.claim: Quick Start: `/writ "users can't paste into the search box on Safari"` restates Goal, Problem, and Done check, proposes `/prototype --no-diverge (Recommended)`, asks one confirmation, then runs.
Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add sellke/writ` then `claude plugin install writ@writ` installs Writ (user scope, cache copy).
Claude Code plugin: run `/writ:initialize` to create the `.writ/` workspace.
Claude Code plugin: every command carries the `writ:` prefix, so the front door is `/writ:writ`.
Claude Code plugin: scripts run from the plugin's own folder, so the project needs no `scripts/` copy.
Claude Code plugin: the `.writ/docs/` reference docs that install.sh copies are not included (DEV-006).
Cursor plugin: copying `cursor/plugin/.` to `~/.cursor/plugins/local/writ` and reloading loads Writ's rule, commands, and skills.
Cursor plugin: commands run `python3 scripts/<name>.py` in the project, so the user also runs the Cursor one-line install.
Cursor (install.sh): after the one-line install, `/writ "my feature"` in Cursor chat runs the front door.
Claude Code (install.sh): after the one-line install, `/writ "my feature"` runs the front door.
Codex: after install and a restart, asking Codex to follow `.codex/commands/writ.md` runs `/writ "my feature"`.
Install sections are ordered by the recorded smoke results; a failing Cursor plugin target removes the `### Cursor (plugin)` subsection.
Quick Start points a new user to `.writ/docs/prompting-guide.md` before the route table.
Every install.sh project gets `.writ/docs/prompting-guide.md`.
The guide reads in two minutes and covers the three request parts, five recipes with routes, and five pitfalls, with no links.
`/writ` restates a request as labeled Goal, Problem, Done check, and Proof lines in Writ's words, and names a missing part instead of asking for it.
The labeled lines print first every time, even when the session already holds context (rule added in 1dcb44c after UAT).

`/writ` routes by the six-row table: a bug to `/prototype --no-diverge`, a capability to `/create-spec`, an unsettled idea to `/prototype`, a named phase to `/implement-phase <N>`, a why question to `/research`, a fork to `/prototype` with the fork named; a rename stays on `--no-diverge`.
One confirmation: the proposed route first with `(Recommended)`, every other table route as an option, `Not what I meant` last.
Picking `Not what I meant` asks one free-text question, then restates and routes again.
After confirmation, the routed command's phase headings go on the native todo list before it runs, with skipped phases marked `skip: <reason>`.
Where the adapter maps `todo_write` to a file write (Codex), `/writ` prints the phases as a markdown checklist and writes nothing.
`/writ` writes nothing under `.writ/` itself.
With no request `/writ` asks "What do you want to do?"; with no goal it asks one natural-language question before routing.
With no roadmap, the restatement says so and names `/plan-product`, and `/implement-phase` is not offered.
When the routed command file is missing (partial install), `/writ` names the file and `/update-writ` and does not improvise the workflow.
`/writ @file` reads an issue file as the request, and `--from-issue <path>` travels to `/create-spec`.
Headless `claude -p "/writ ..."` restates and proposes a route as a numbered list and runs nothing.

Under the Claude Code plugin, the routed command (`/writ:prototype`, `/writ:create-spec`) runs to completion in a plugin-only project, including commands that cite `.writ/docs/` files the plugin does not ship.
Under the plugin, `/writ:initialize` Step 0 runs `scaffold-writ.py` from the plugin root before detection, reports each created line, and stops on a failing scaffold.
In an install.sh project or under the Cursor plugin, Step 0 runs `python3 scripts/scaffold-writ.py` from the project's `scripts/`.
Greenfield detection counts the `.writ/` tree Step 0 created as boilerplate, so a new project is not read as brownfield.
On Claude Code, `/create-spec` discovery enters Plan Mode by itself through `EnterPlanMode`, presents the contract as the plan, and asks the Contract Decision after plan exit.
`/plan-product` and `/new-command` discovery enter Plan Mode through the adapter's `Plan Mode` row.
Plan Mode on other platforms: Cursor asks the user to switch to Plan Mode and waits; Codex and OpenClaw run discovery as a read-only conversation and say so.
The Plan Mode row tells the agent to open the contract plan with one line saying approval accepts the draft and runs nothing (47137a1).
`todo_write` maps to the native `TodoWrite` list, so routed phases mirror there and no tracking file is written.
On Claude Code desktop, `/prototype --diverge` drafts render as an artifact or in the Browser pane.

Under the plugin, read-only agent spawns stay read-only (the adapter's `Task({ readonly: true })` row maps them to `permissionMode: plan` plus `disallowedTools` and says "Enforced at tool level"), although the adapter says plugin agents ignore `permissionMode`.
With install.sh and the plugin in one project, both command sets exist and a project command does not shadow the plugin's.

The plugin's Prime Directive carrier holds when the user has their own output style or another plugin forces one; the adapter warns that the user's style is overridden and the first loaded forced style wins.
A headless `claude -p` `/prototype` run has artifacts off and takes the no-renderer path.
Codex CLI `/prototype --diverge` writes one self-contained HTML file per draft under `.writ/prototypes/<date>-<slug>/` and says the drafts were not rendered.
Codex Desktop: rendering an HTML draft is not documented, so the agent writes the same files.
`file_search` maps to `Glob("**/pattern*")`, a built-in Glob tool, on Codex.
An install.sh Cursor project gets 33 commands in `.cursor/commands/`, `writ.md` among them.
Cursor plugin agents carry generated `name` and `description` frontmatter and Cursor lists them as agents (DEV-017 fix, d8b9f17).
On Cursor, `/prototype` writes one HTML file per draft; the Browser tool renders a draft only from an allowlisted served origin; otherwise the agent says the drafts were not rendered.
OpenClaw: `canvas-preview` writes one HTML file per draft and sends each path; `Task({ readonly: true })` adds a no-modify constraint to the prompt; Plan Mode runs as a read-only conversation.
The installed CLAUDE.md Writ block says "Start with `/writ`" above the Commands table and lists `/writ`.
The installed CLAUDE.md carries the Claude Code Capability Map, and the installed agent resolves Writ's capability names from it with no `adapters/` present.
The installed map's `AskQuestion` row (formatted numbered text, "No interactive UI") matches Claude Code.
The AGENTS.md Writ block lists all 33 commands with `/writ` first under "Start here", the 8 agents, and the 16 skills, with their install paths.
The AGENTS.md block carries the Codex Capability Map and names no `adapters/` path, so a Codex agent maps tools without adapter files.
A Codex install gives the agent Writ's identity and Prime Directive: the AGENTS.md block says "Read bundled `system-instructions.md` for Writ identity".
The Writ block stays under 16 KiB, inside Codex's 32 KiB default AGENTS.md budget.
The generated `.cursor/rules/writ.mdc` (alwaysApply) still carries the whole of `system-instructions.md`, so Cursor sessions keep the Prime Directive.
The rule carries the Cursor Capability Map, and a Cursor agent resolves Writ's capability names from it.
`/create-issue` and `/writ-design` name neutral capabilities (`codebase_search`, `file_search`, the platform's browser tool) that each platform's map resolves.
`/status` may suggest `/writ` among its next actions.
SKILL.md lists `/writ` first under "Start here", regenerated from the manifest.
`/writ` is registered in the `entry` category ("Start here"), and every catalog regenerates from it.
`/writ` declares `entry_level: high`.
`scaffold-writ.py` follows the check-shape CLI contract (verdict line, reason lines, summary).
install.sh creates the eleven `.writ/` directories and adds `.writ/state/` and `.writ-lanes-*/` to `.gitignore`, byte for byte as scaffold-writ.py does.
install.sh does not ship `gen-platform-trees.py` into projects.
`install.sh --platform claude` gives the agent the Prime Directive through the CLAUDE.md Writ block's `@.claude/system-instructions.md` import.
update.sh repairs a missing `.writ/` directory or `.gitignore` entry on every non-dry run and leaves the `.gitignore` change uncommitted.
update.sh keeps `gen-platform-trees.py` out of updated projects.
unlink.sh's shippable-script rule matches install.sh and update.sh.
`scaffold-writ.py scaffold` creates the tree, a second run creates nothing, and `--check` writes nothing.
Maintainer: `--check` fails on a stale, missing, orphan, unmapped, or vendor hit, and write mode regenerates every platform tree and both plugins.
Maintainer: gen-claude-md renders the "Start with `/writ`" line and the capability map into `claude-code/CLAUDE.md`, and `--check` passes.
Maintainer: eval.sh reports each platform-trees reason as one finding, pins `writ.md`'s Routing Rules heading and `entry_level`, skips `plugins/` for leanness, and reports 0 findings on the branch.
The forced output style `output-styles/writ.md` carries the Prime Directive: a plugin session quotes the first Hard Constraints bullet and names its persona Writ; without the plugin it has none.
Only the eight generated `writ:*` agents load; the prompt-template docs and `_preamble.md` register nothing; 33 commands and 16 skills load.
The plugin passes `claude plugin validate` (warnings only: eight no-frontmatter prompt docs and a missing icon).
Under the plugin, commands that call scripts act on the user's project, not on the plugin folder.
No dev-only script (install, update, eval, gen-platform-trees) ships in the plugin.
In a Cursor plugin session `rules/writ.mdc` (byte-equal to `cursor/writ.mdc`) loads always-apply and the Prime Directive is visible (V76).
`/writ` and the other commands from `commands/` appear in Cursor (V77).
`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` carries name and version from VERSION and no component path field, so Cursor discovers the default folders.
The repository root is a Claude Code marketplace named `writ` that lists plugin `writ` at `./plugins/writ`.
